findings.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.java:71: canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, allowing administrators with only all-groups view permission to pass requireManage() and create groups; it must require MANAGE exclusively.

UsersResource.java:451: Setting UserModel.GROUPS restricts searches to permitted groups, excluding individually authorized users outside those groups before permission evaluation; searches must include users authorized individually or through group membership.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.java:451: Setting UserModel.GROUPS restricts searches to permitted groups, excluding individually authorized users outside those groups before permission evaluation; searches must include users authorized individually or through group membership.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in UsersResource.java:451, the code now unconditionally sets UserModel.GROUPS when groupIds is not empty, regardless of whether the user has canView() permission. Previously (lines 448-454 in the old code), it only set this attribute when `!auth.users().canView()`. The new code removes this check, meaning even users with full view permission will have their searches restricted to group members. Additionally, the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` was removed from line 457, which previously allowed individually authorized users to pass through. This combination could exclude users who are authorized individually but not through group membership.
